newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-France Telecom sale seen in September.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France Telecom sale seen in September.

text.p: France could offer a minority stake in France Telecom for sale in September, relaunching what could be the country's biggest ever market float, an official source said on Thursday.

But the Socialist-led government, elected two months ago partly on an election plank of opposing privatisations, will stress the move is important for the company's future in a competitive environment and that the sale does not signal a continuation of the conservative government's asset sale programme.

The official source, who declined to be identified, said the decision to sell would be announced as soon as a report by state envoy Michel Delebarre was handed to the government. This is expected before September 5.
A spokesman for the Finance Ministry said no decision had been taken and that the government was awaiting the Delebarre report.

France Telecom, whose value was estimated in April at between 160 billion ($25.9 billion) and 210 billion francs, is the biggest of the companies that were on the conservative government's privatisation list.
Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has in the past few weeks stopped the sale of defence electronics group Thomson-CSF and said consumer electronics group Thomson Multimedia would remain in state hands.

The government decided to go ahead with the privatisation of insurance company GAN and its banking unit CIC in order to get permission on Wednesday from the European Union for 23.7 billion francs in state aid to the company.
The government is also expected to yield to the European Union's demands to privatise bank Credit Lyonnais.
The future of airline Air France is less clear. Company chairman Christian Blanc, who advocates a rapid sale, met with Jospin last week.

Communist Transport minister Claude Gayssot told RTL radio on Thursday he was opposed to a privatisation of Air France. "I do not believe that a privatisation is the best solution for the future of that company," he said.
The conservative government had planned to sell a stake of some 35 percent of France Telecom in an Initial Public Offering in the spring with the aim of raising between 30 and 50 billion francs.
In a second stage the group could swap a 10 percent stake with Deutsche Telekom to cement the Global One alliance, which also includes Sprint, to better compete against BT/MCI and AT&T.
The sale was postponed from May to June after President Jacques Chirac called snap elections and the procedure was suspended altogether when the Left won the elections.
Jospin had promised during his campaign to consult the staff of France Telecom before taking any decision on a sale.
Delebarre was appointed on July 17 to lead a "wide consultation" of France Telecom staff and management about all issues concerning the company's future, including a possible sale.
Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said at the time that the state would keep a majority stake in France Telecom and that the company would keep its current legal status.

Since January 1, France Telecom SA has been a state-owned company with a share capital. Before that, it was a state service. France Telecom employees may keep their status as civil servants, including a job guarantee and a relatively good pension.

The previous government struck a deal with France Telecom under which it took over the pension liabilities of the civil servants at the company, in exchange for a one-off payment of 37.5 billion francs. That was used to reduce the 1997 budget deficit to better qualify for the Maastricht criteria for European monetary union.
Proceeds from the sale of state assets may not be used to reduce the deficit under European rules.
Delebarre met the main unions at France Telecom and on Wednesday evening said the staff's main concern was the uncertain outlook.

He declined to give his position on a possible sale but said, "I am not among those people who believe that an opening of the capital (sale of a minority stake) is a privatisation." -- Marcel Michelson and William Emmanuel, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
($ = 6.184 French Francs)
